name: NY-25
label: Safe D

key_factors: Morelle is an incumbent in a D+10 district with a roughly $1.8M-to-$32K fundraising advantage
Challenger McIntyre has minimal cash and no outside support, while Morelle has outside backing and no opposing spending
Polymarket prices Democrats at about 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so evidence is limited to fundamentals and markets
model.rationale: Morelle holds a D+10 seat, a massive financial edge over a minimally funded challenger, outside support with no opposition spending, and markets price Democrats near 96 percent, all consistent with a safe incumbent win.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Morelle or any new polling showing a single-digit race would be the first sign of trouble, but nothing of the kind is currently visible.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joseph Morelle, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Rochester-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. He has raised roughly $1.8 million and enjoys more than half a million dollars in outside support, while Republican Virginia McIntyre has raised about $32,000 with little cash on hand. No outside groups are spending against Morelle, and no public polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 96 percent, and the district's partisan lean points strongly toward the incumbent. With no public polling or expert ratings of the race, expectations rest on the district's fundamentals and the stark resource gap between the candidates. An upset would require a dramatic and unforeseen shift; the available evidence points to a comfortable Morelle victory.
